review_note: Preserve the experimental role swap; distinguish it from validation of the course's numerical rule.

edits.before: Week 9 had been asserting two things this study tests. First, that listening is a move rather than a pause between moves — the listeners were the ones whose liking went up, which is Collins and Miller's third effect produced experimentally rather than meta-analysed. Second, and more useful, that the course's plus-or-minus-one rule is about *both* people stepping. Here is what a one-sided exchange produces: an asymmetry in how the two people feel about it. And here is what fixes it: taking the other turn. The rate limit is not politeness. It is the mechanism by which two people end up in the same conversation.
edits.after: Week 9 uses the role swap to discuss reciprocity: the two participants' impressions changed when each had taken both turns. It is a reason to attend to who gets to disclose and who gets to listen. The study does not test the course's plus-or-minus-one rule.
edits.reason: Keep the teaching use without claiming the study tests the course's numerical model or proves a universal repair.
